Republic of South Africa

IN THE LABOUR COURT OF SOUTH AFRICA, JOHANNESBURG

Not Reportable

Case no: JR 1487/21

In the matter between:

THEMBA MAHLANGU                    Applicant

and

SIBANYE GOLD LIMITED t/a SIBANYE-STILLWATER          First Respondent

COMMISSION FOR CONCILIATION, MEDIATION AND ARBITRATION          Second Respondent

COMMISSIONER N P DLAMINI N.O.                    Third Respondent

Heard: 8 May 2024

Delivered: 14 June 2024

JUDGMENT

VAN NIEKERK J

[1] This is an application brought in terms of section 145 of the Labour Relations Act 66 of 1995 (the LRA) to review and set aside an arbitration award issued by the third respondent under the auspices of the CCMA.

[2] The applicant was employed by the first respondent as a rock drill operator at its gold mine. He worked underground in a stoping crew. He was dismissed on 3 February 2021 following a disciplinary hearing on a charge of a breach of a safety rule, namely failing to conduct a gas test before charging up a face.

[3] It was common cause that the employer applies a zero tolerance policy to breaches of what it terms cardinal rules. The chairperson of the enquiry testified that once the breach was established he had no discretion.

[4] The applicant contended that the charge sheet was vague and that the charge on which he was found guilty differed from the charge put to him at the outset.

[5] The applicant further testified that he was denied representation by his shop steward and that no interpreter was made available, although his home language is isiZulu.

[6] Two other employees in the same crew were not dismissed for the same conduct. The commissioner did not deal with this inconsistency at all.

[7] The Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996 imposes real duties on an employer to maintain a safe working environment. That does not relieve an employer of the obligation to consider whether dismissal is an appropriate sanction in the circumstances of the individual employee.

[8] Applying Sidumo, the question is whether the award is one that a reasonable decision-maker could reach. The commissioner failed to apply his mind to the applicant's length of service and clean disciplinary record.

[9] In the result I find that the dismissal was procedurally unfair and that the award falls to be set aside.

Order

[10] The arbitration award is reviewed and set aside.

[11] The applicant is reinstated with retrospective effect to the date of dismissal.

[12] There is no order as to costs.

VAN NIEKERK J
Judge of the Labour Court of South Africa
